headline: Maui Has 45,737 Kūpuna Over 60

meeting.summary: The Council on Aging heard about Lānaʻi home health care, a needs survey for the four-year plan, and an older adult's contractor fraud case.
meeting.recap: Nine members were present, enough for a quorum (the minimum needed to hold the meeting).[[0:06:52]] Members voted on the June 9th minutes.[[0:09:56]] A Lānaʻi home health agency said it is the only licensed one on the island that it knows of.[[0:12:45]] The agency said it averages about 40 clients at a time with limited staff.[[0:18:33]] The agency is planning a licensed adult day care for 10 clients to start.[[0:24:49]] Staff said 14 kūpuna were honored at a luncheon for their volunteer work.[[0:38:20]] Staff said Maui County has 45,737 people age 60 and over.[[1:03:18]] A member said a budget freeze left many seniors on wait lists.[[1:27:35]] The office reported seven staff vacancies.[[1:35:40]] The office said home-delivered meals serve at least 600 participants.[[1:38:23]] The next meeting is August 11 at 12:30.[[1:50:08]]
decided: A motion to send the topic prioritization survey to members was made, members said aye, and no result was announced.
meeting.next: Office staff will reach out to set up a focus group with the disability community. Council members will be told the focus group schedule once it is set. The office hopes recruitment for three positions goes out within the next couple weeks.

moments.q: Maui County population age 60 and over
